# The v2 SEAL-TEL wire contract (NWP-20261022-11): the request the chooser sends and the replies it reads.
# BOTH suites read this one file, so an edit here is an edit to the wire:
#   - Go:   core/agent/tel_wire_contract_test.go  (readSealTelV2, okArrivalReply, errNobodyReply)
#   - Java: core/chooser/tests/tel-wire/TelWireCases.java  (TelArrival.telRequest, smsId, callId, parse, untilAnswered)
# One case per line; fields are separated by a TAB and an empty field is a real empty value. Lines starting with # and
# blank lines are ignored. Every field writes a backslash as \\, a newline as \n and a tab as \t (any other backslash
# sequence is an error), so a value may hold any of them.
#
# REQ-TEL  type, case, aid, kind, sub, iccid, from, when, mono, body, callType, durSec, request
#   aid      the arrival id: TelArrival.smsId(sub, when, from, body) for kind sms, TelArrival.callId(sub, when) for call
#   from, body   the decoded values (the request carries them as base64)
#   when     the arrival time in ms; mono the SystemClock.elapsedRealtime stamp (they differ, so a swap shows)
#   request  the exact bytes TelArrival.telRequest sends, which readSealTelV2 must read back as the other columns
# REPLY    type, case, line, kind, vis, label, sealed, liveUid, stripped, partial
#   line     one reply line without its newline
#   kind, vis, label (decoded), liveUid (-1 for none), stripped (0 or 1), partial (0 or 1)  what TelArrival.parse(line) must yield
#   sealed   the count okArrivalReply is given for an OK line, - on any other line (it is also given stripped and partial)
